label: Unit 2
intro: Put the play coins on the table and give each one a place: save, spend or give. Keep the totals small enough to check by hand. The giving jar has a person at the other end, and we thank God for what we have.

gelds.text: Counting on and backward to twenty-one
Waiting for a goal and recounting after spending
Giving to help someone and thanking God

tryNote: Use large pretend coins. Agree on any paid extra job before it starts; ordinary family helping still belongs to all of us.

daily.title: Give every coin one home
daily.do: Count six play coins into save, spend and give jars. He chooses where each goes. One coin cannot be in two jars.
daily.stretch: Build the pile to twenty-one, count backward, then compare two piles one apart; before moving one coin, he predicts each new total and checks it.

daily.title: Agree before the job
daily.do: Name a normal family job, then agree on one extra job and its pretend pay. He does the extra job and counts the coins with you. The agreement comes first.
daily.stretch: He explains why ordinary helping was not a paid deal, chooses a savings goal, and says how many more coins it needs after putting his earnings away.
daily.skill: An earning agreement and a savings gap

daily.title: Spend one, give one
daily.do: Price a pretend item at one coin; he pays from the spend jar and recounts. Then name someone the give jar could help.
daily.stretch: He predicts what remains before paying, keeps the pretend private key to himself, and chooses a gift with a reason it helps; finish by thanking God together.
daily.skill: Planning a choice and protecting private information

goalsTitle: What he should have by the end of this unit

his: Counts a collection to 21, counts backward, and compares two counted piles one apart.
Names an agreed extra job that earns money and distinguishes it from ordinary family helping.
Divides play coins among save, spend, and give and explains that the same coin cannot go in two jars.
Waits toward a named savings goal, recounts after spending one coin, and keeps the private-key rule when pretending to pay.
Chooses someone to help with the giving jar, says how the gift helps, and thanks God for what he has.

weekend: Choose one real giving plan together, with a grown-up handling the money. Let him name who it helps and say the thank-you prayer; the amount is your decision.

songs.title: Three Little Jars
songs.style: Start singing immediately, with no instrumental intro. Warm acoustic guitar, soft bass and a gentle swaying rhythm. One clear warm voice, short repeated melody, steady preschool pace, clean ending without a long outro.
lyrics: Save a little, spend with care.
Give a little, we can share.
Thank You, God, for what we hold.
Help us give with hearts of gold.
One coin here, one coin there.
One coin cannot be a pair.
Count what's left and let it stay.
Earn the pay we first agreed.
Save a little, spend with care.
Give a little, we can share.

basic.label: Coin
basic.note: Count each coin once before choosing a jar.

basic.label: Jar
basic.note: A jar holds the coins you put aside.

basic.label: Gift
basic.note: A gift goes to somebody else.

basic.label: Basket
basic.note: A basket can hold the things you plan to buy.

basic.label: Apple
basic.note: An apple can be something on a shopping list.

basic.label: Toy car
basic.note: A toy car can be a named savings goal.

advanced.label: Save jar
advanced.note: Coins in the save jar wait for a goal.

advanced.label: Spend jar
advanced.note: Coins in the spend jar can pay for a planned purchase.

advanced.label: Give jar
advanced.note: Coins in the give jar help someone else.

advanced.label: Job agreement
advanced.note: Agree with a grown-up on an extra job and its pay before starting.

advanced.label: Price tag
advanced.note: The price tag tells how much the item costs.

advanced.label: Receipt
advanced.note: A receipt records what was bought.

advanced.label: Private key
advanced.note: A private key stays private; it can unlock your money.

advanced.label: Savings goal
advanced.note: A savings goal names what you are waiting to buy.

items.text: You put a coin aside for a toy you will buy later.
items.note: That coin waits for the toy goal.

items.text: You pay one coin for the pretend apple now.
items.note: That coin pays for something now.

items.text: You leave three coins in the save jar for later.
items.note: The coins stay put for a later choice.

items.text: You hand the shopkeeper two coins for a book.
items.note: The coins leave to pay for the book.

items.text: You add your extra-job coin to the bike fund.
items.note: You are building the pile for the bike.

items.text: You pay for a snack with the spend jar.
items.note: You are using coins to buy the snack.

items.text: You count the toy fund and put every coin back.
items.note: Counting did not spend any of the saved coins.

items.text: You buy a pencil with one of your coins.
items.note: The coin pays for the pencil.

items.text: You wait and keep the money for your named goal.
items.note: Waiting leaves the money saved.

items.text: You move saved money to a different jar but keep it for the same goal.
items.note: A different container did not turn the money into a purchase.

items.text: You take a coin from the save jar and pay for a toy today.
items.note: The jar name does not change the act of buying.

items.text: You use the spend jar coin to start saving for a later book.
items.note: This time you put the coin aside instead of buying.

items.text: You buy the toy after saving for weeks.
items.note: The waiting was saving; paying today is spending.

items.text: You pay for a cheaper toy and still have coins left.
items.note: Paying is spending even when some money remains.

sort.title: Safe to Give or Share?
sort.sub: Safe to share or Keep it private

items.text: With Dad, you give the agreed gift coins to the food collection.
items.note: Dad helps the gift reach the collection.

items.text: You tell a stranger your private key.
items.note: A private key can unlock your money.

items.text: You tell a friend your favorite color.
items.note: A favorite color does not unlock an account.

items.text: You send a game player your home address.
items.note: Your home address stays with trusted grown-ups.

items.text: You give Mom the drawing you made for her.
items.note: You chose to give your own drawing.

items.text: You tell a stranger your account password.
items.note: Passwords belong with you and your trusted grown-up.

items.text: With Mom, you give your chosen toy to the family collection.
items.note: Mom helps with giving a toy you chose.

items.text: You post the door code in a game chat.
items.note: A door code lets someone into a private place.

items.text: You tell a friend you saved five play coins.
items.note: A pretend coin count is not a private key.

items.text: A stranger promises to pay you after you send your private key.
items.note: A promise of money does not make the private key safe to share.

items.text: You show a pretend price of three coins on your shop sign.
items.note: A shop price is meant for customers to see.

items.text: A game asks for your address to send a free gift, and you type it in.
items.note: Ask your grown-up instead of giving the game your address.

items.text: With Dad beside you, you hand over the agreed donation without showing a password.
items.note: Giving the gift does not require sharing your password.

items.text: Someone says the secret code is needed for charity, and you send it.
items.note: Helping someone does not mean handing out a secret code.
